description: Shared Renovate preset of the repositories of this account, used as local>magicsunday/.github:renovate-config.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A pull request for a known vulnerability carries its own label, so it stands out from the weekly updates.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Weekly refresh of the lock files, so a package that only a lock file holds gets updated. A refresh has no release timestamp, so the age wait is optional here and cannot hold back a freshly published release of a transitive package. This risk is accepted on purpose. The pull request merges by itself once the required checks of the repository pass, so those checks are its only gate.

customManagers.description: The tooling image that a workflow receives as its node-image input, so the digest pin reaches CI as well as the Compose file.
The default of the node-image input in the shared workflows of this repository.

packageRules.description: One grouped pull request per package manager.
The Python version of the workflows is pinned on purpose, because the hash-locked pip closures are compiled for it, so a human moves it.

The shared workflows of this repository are called with the @main ref by policy, so they stay unpinned and a change of a shared workflow reaches every consumer at once. Every other action keeps its digest pin.

Patch, minor and digest updates of GitHub Actions merge by themselves once the required checks pass and the age wait is over. Renovate performs the merge itself, because a merge by the platform would not wait for the age check, which is no required status check. Major updates stay with a human.

Patch and minor updates of npm packages merge by themselves once the required checks pass and the age wait is over. Renovate performs the merge itself, for the reason given for GitHub Actions. The age wait applies where the registry gives a release date, and the git tag pins of the account are taken without it, see the last rule. Major updates stay with a human. An update that changes a committed bundle gets a commit of the bundle job on its branch. Renovate may treat that as a manual edit of the branch and leave the pull request open for a person, and the rules here do not decide that.
The chart library bundle is baked into the committed minified files at build time, so it arrives as its own pull request that carries the rebuilt bundle.
Every reference to the tooling image moves in one pull request, so the local build and CI keep using the same image.

A new digest of the tooling image merges by itself once the required checks pass. The catalogue checks run with the new image. The bundle check does not guard against a changed image on a pull request of Renovate, because the bundle job commits the rebuilt files to that branch. A new tag of the image stays with a human.

The digest of the tooling image stays with a human in this repository. Its required checks do not run the image, and the default of the shared workflows reaches every consumer at once, while in a consumer the catalogue checks run with the new image before the merge. This rule comes after the one above so that it wins.

The hash-locked pip closures are compiled per Python version, so their weekly refresh stays with a human, whatever the switch of the lock file refresh says. This rule comes after that switch so that it wins.
Registries other than Docker Hub, ghcr.io among them, publish no release timestamp, so image updates would never count as old enough.
Pins by git tag are taken without the age wait.
